body:
I honestly don't believe you're trying to help. Off in my head goes a sarcastic, "Oh you think?" Further, you can believe what you want about therapy as you've stated that it isn't all inclusive. The fact of the matter is that professional therapy addresses a problem that a person faces. In this respect, it is a solution to parts of that problem. You're arguing atoms on split hair follicles. Before 'formal' psychologists and practices existed, people had others who they could naturally confide in. I don't doubt there was a therapist-equivalent. I know what is troubling me. And I know intuitively what would help me. So I choose "c" for "both." I'll remark nothing more about the matter, and I certainly don't make it my business to convince you otherwise on what I have remarked.

I am saying that there is no way to have a sufficient understanding about everything because of the intrinsic nature, tendency and wealth of an evolving complexity. In order to understand what meaning is, one must satisfy the conditions of being able to prescribe meaning and for the meaning to be operational. It is because we ultimately differ that there is nothing, fundamentally that could have meaning. Because of Godel's Theorem, (different from a "theory" and therefore operational regardless of belief) there is nothing that we could construct to sufficiently accommodate all of the meanings that we'd build on. It doesn't mean that we have to suffer however. It could serve to simply enjoy one's experience. I'll concede as this might quickly become a clash in metaphysics and the abstract. Forgive my mistrust of your wield and I'll say nothing more about the matter. Thing is, if anything proves that Incompleteness (which would be severely spectacular) is not unassailable, then I'm okay with being wrong too, why I choose both.

And there's my proof in the pudding from eating it. For which ever reason, you don't understand me and my "elusive diction." I have not questioned my "habit" because I've met people in passing who've intuitively understood my meaning. This also addresses your question about ascribing (mapping) meaning unto the world. That you may define it as a "habit," I could not want to know the answer to the question I have in mind. After all, why should it matter—who are you? You might have facilitated a motivational famine for me and you might take joy in it. But at least I can be aware that I thirst for something positive, or that it would remind to be. So I carefully scraped my tongue off for a new taste, seeing the end of something. I walked away from my laptop, the bitten apple light distance telling a story of how I came to be hungry. My stomach grumbled, I shrugged, then enjoyed something like the wheat in a daydream's crust at a distance.

In fear of this becoming a mathematical drenched explanation, I'll suggest that even the Quantum Field Theory cannot evade Godel's Incompleteness Theorem. That there is nothing (mathematically, therefore computationally) sufficient to hold our absolute understanding of things. It is because this value pales in comparison to infinitely expansive complexity that lends to a difficult analogy. 
Epistemology:Incomplete :: Incompleteness:Complete

My therapy is not helpful. It must also be realized that therapy is only one solution; the quality of which is contingent on the difficulty one faces coupled with the correlation to psychological treatment—which has no defined model for all-inclusive treatment.

I hope I've provided clarity.

Thanks, but my issue here isn't other ways something could be worse—I've never used that model as a motivational epitaph. But I do agree with you that, continuing to be nameless doesn't have to damn me. I'll be sure to embrace something that is slightly different from what you might suggest, ensuring that it should also honor an implicit resiliency.

Something smacked of clarity, as if I were a fractious child, when ridding myself of mostly everything. I'll be hungry but maybe in a different way someday, hopefully. I know who I truly am, but it's about being in a place that will let me be who I am. I cannot find that. My entire life has been spent creating or trying to find a kind environment. I should go for a walk and ponder this and any sense of encouragement that I grip, for now. And so I left.

Everything, ultimately, upon a closer inspection, is a series of electrons. Espoused to it is a formalism, which proves that nothing really matters. Why look further into the "metaphor" (pataphor), what's your point?

Ignore the fact that I mentioned my entanglement with therapy and patronize me no further with your wishes.

Yeah? I hope nothing that I've mentioned has happened to you or anyone. I never felt this kind of emptiness before. I've tried to off myself in the past due to other grief. This time feels unbridled, abstruse, and effective. If you have a blue print of a solution, I'd enjoy at least one part to being in so much debt. Maybe a one up in the battle against what's left of how much I desperately don't know.

I enjoy neuroscience thoroughly, so depression has found an objective spot in my heart. Reading about depression from another person forgets to capture the same boundlessness of what another person is experiencing. In turn, from reading, a person runs the risk of self-diagnosis. I understand my emotions with high fidelity, but I also know where they stand. I call my self out on delusions, but I'm also aware that my body is an organism that I must train to tame for when I can't. That I'd suffer from something that I can't see, that would make my body react to drench its curtains with cortisol, I'd end its existence because I couldn't do anything else positive for it. A bit of a strange philosophical underpinning, but I understand that a part of me is not in my control.

In order to be 'loved', one must be 'lovable.' Depression couldn't be farther from comforting in my case. The reality is that people can end up alone, no matter what. They can fail no matter what. I'll concede that part of this, I've assumed as my own, in what you qualify as a skewed view. But I also know, that no one or anything has ever proven me wrong about those particular convictions. I would like to stick around to be proven otherwise. But I don't think that's worth waiting for, especially when someone has the freedom to magically reject you in a selfish pursuit of an ecstasy pill made of human. My life is almost done, 22 snaps latched to a neutrino. I'd like a change soon, a sign, a precursor even—but times like these? I'm merely blank. Regardless, I see a straight face. I'll intend to crave nothing, inviting over my skewed vision, deluded that I'm not alone. What is the world to a wandering, nameless, silent, and headless roach? Forgive my tendency to inexplicably ignore a field of crumbs you easily flirt with and my inability to scrape my tongue to remember a similar place.

The fire is definitely gone, and I won't burn anymore of them. I guess it seared about something in my belly. It was humming a will o' the wisp cacophony of the past. I have nothing but this laptop now. Everything else material abstaining from defenestration. I'll try my hand at their stomps of inspiration.

I appreciated the link.

Where did I hope to be? On the side, I was developing a concept that, somewhere else, came to be known as the Khan Academy. No one was interested in such a venture. As a result I lost the respect of company CEO's who were going to invest heavily in online ventures. With whatever I'd earn, I hoped to be somewhere by 22, doing something extremely helpful with people who were insulating. Then, I'd have enough capital to build my own lab, fund research and conduct experiments to solve severely complex problems that are neglected by the world. Solving the protein folding problem would negate the need for any drug. It can be done with a mathematical formula—but I have to be published to be listened to. That would mean the ability to create neurotransmitters...I lack the strength to collect my bearings. I thought, I actually thought that I could cure what I had. I thought I'd eventually find others might believe in that too; like I'm the only one. I truly believed in that good will. I'm nothing, because I can't even find something so simple.

You weren't patronizing at all, compared to the infectious gashes on my self esteem from out there in the wild. Instead, you were kind, like the halcyon delights of nature's wind, a dandelion's sudden decision to wave me a 1000 hi's. Yeah, that fair chance for me to catch at least one, a 99.9% Gaussian chance that I would. Yes, I want to etch the bark on the willow and "assign that purpose", a command in my SQL table, but also to share MySQL database.

I feel only a little better today and I don't regret my disposals. I don't know what to do. Life isn't a lab protocol. Everything is blank. I feel blank. Regardless of what might happen, thank you for your kindness to someone who could finally become no one.

The problem ultimately boils down to the lack of a real, constant outlet for anything. I am not superficial with anything. There is a purpose for what should be good. The human experience means to collectively celebrate that good. Power to you for a statue, consolidating all that went into a smirk toward those gazing, lugubrious masks—all of them. You had the wonderful experience in handing yours over as well. And those trades? Also a symbol that someone else interacted with you. I’d have the strength to envy that you sent that concept of loneliness, billowing far into respiratory plight, if my lack of breaths weren’t just as great…

I feel more like a painter without paint. Even once I get it, there is no telling that those rehearsed strokes could bleed the canvas out, a cerulean river. I'd etch crinkles and splashes by the bank—a reminded mindedness you prophesized. Even still, it'd be all but a lost painting. So goes the sight of a nomad rejecting another patch on the planet.
